title: Seratonin Syndrome?
selftext: 20 year old male, 6’2” 165lbs. I’ve been suffering with pretty severe anxiety and panic attacks regarding my health and I realize that this question is most likely rooted in my anxiety but I’d rather be safe than sorry. My doctor prescribed me 50 mg sertraline with directions to take half a pill (25 mg) a day for the first 7 days then move up to the full 50mg. She also prescribed me 15 mg buspirone with directions to take 1/2 a pill to 1 full pill twice daily. I’ve been taking both of my meds for about a week now and have been noticing headaches and ringing in much ears at night as well as stiff muscles, dry mouth, slight memory impairment,  and dilated pupils. I’m nervous to take the meds anymore due to the possibility of getting seratonin syndrome because of mixing two serstonin-related drugs. My question is: do I have anything to be worried about on my dosages and combining these two or am I overthinking?

title: Alprazolam Mylan, I'm a bit paranoid if I got placebo or not.
selftext:
So I have anxiety where I leave the house and I end up puking, I stay with anxiety in bed just thinking about leaving (due to school). I have anxiety because I have chronic pain from something that has yet to be diagnosed which makes me feel worthless and tired all the time for my age and that maybe I can't achieve the normal life my friends will have.

I'm 20 yo and a female.

At first my doctor got the Alprazolam Mylan ones that were oval and a bit orangy/pink in that little green metallic container or wtv you call it (I'm foreigner), tasted very bad, they were 0.5 mg. Those did nothing, I used them like in 4 months, it depended on how I was doing, and he gave me boxes of 20 units. They did absolutely nothing to me, I never used more then 0.5mg in a day.

So I told him, this isn't working and he just said ok and upped to 1mg, I told him if he could give me a larger package because I'm a college student and going to the doctor and spending money everytime I went there to get a new prescription was hurting my wallet.

Without any trouble he gave me a box of 60 pills, I'm really surprised at this point at how a doctor can be so irresponsible. Same green container inside the box, oval pills, now they are blue with a G ''stamped'' on it. But I really don't feel any effect, I function normally and still feel this huge panic sometimes when going outside or going to school.

I'm starting to become paranoid that maybe he is giving me placebo, considering he is willing to prescribe me a box of like 60 of them and all the supposed alprazolam pills he gave me cost like 3 dollar max each box (portugal).

title: Unusual Question About Opioids and Benzodiazepines
selftext:
I had posted this the other day but was no where near concise enough so I deleted and want to post again, but the cliffs notes version this time

Female, 41, 5’ 5”, obese but losing weight through hard work (down roughly 35 pounds in 5 months), natural redhead 

Complex medical history but pertinent is mitochondrial disease, systemic lupus, dystonia, and severe anxiety; wheelchair dependent; weird genetic processing of medication that makes me very difficult to sedate and rather impervious to the sedating effects of medication

Medications are akin to a small pharmacy but relevant ones are Norco 7.5-325mg every 6-8 hours, Valium 5mg once daily PRN, and Baclofen 20mg 4x day

I receive treatment through palliative care (not hospice but just palliative care) where we are focusing on quality of life as much as quantity of life (because honestly if life is miserable it’s not worth the tremendous fight). My pain medication was recently switched from PRN (where I could make a 1 month supply last 2-3+ months) to scheduled after a rapid decline in the mitochondrial disease precipitated by Covid. I take Baclofen 20 mg 4x day for severe muscle spasms and dystonia. And Valium was added in as needed for a tremendous increase in anxiety and panic attacks (I am already taking Rexulti, Lithium, Buspar, Clonidine, and Trazadone for mental health). The Valium also has an incredible side bonus of helping a bit with the muscle spasms. Given that I am in palliative care with a host of serious illnesses that will likely be life limiting, is this an acceptable treatment approach? I am undergoing the process to see if I qualify for a Baclofen pump for better long term management and am being assessed to see if I have myoclonic dystrophy in addition to everything else.

Thank you for reading my still too long post!

title: What's going on with my shoulder?
selftext:
The last four days, my right shoulder has been causing me pain. I have no idea what I did to aggravate it, it just started hurting out of nowhere. My best guess for the cause is from playing football with my little brother, though it didn't hurt immediately after playing...

Anyway, it's not like my shoulder is completely disabled, but I am a little concerned. If it was just a pulled muscle, shouldn't it have healed by now?

The best way I can describe the pain is this: the pain started in my shoulder blade, but now I notice it more in the armpit area but also the area between my neck and shoulder. It hurts if I make any sudden movements with that side of my body, but then the pain subsides after a moment. If I fully extend my arm forward or upward, it brings a sharp pain to my shoulder for a moment, but then goes away. Then my shoulder will be fine for 3ish minutes, but then it'll hurt to fully extend it again. Carrying anything heavy also hurts for a brief moment, and I feel like the injury is causing me to struggle with carrying things I wouldn't normally struggle to lift. Also, one night while I was trying to sleep, my upper arm was throbbing. I've also had trouble sleeping, although besides that one night, I'm not sure this is related.

I've been trying to take it easy the last few days, but it hasn't gotten better. Maybe it's just a pulled muscle or something, but I've never had such a simple injury take this long to heal. I'm young, so I've always bounced back pretty quickly from minor injuries.

Any insight or advice is appreciated!

title: Advice for bad shoulder
selftext:
44M here.  I'm looking for some help on a situation with my shoulder.   I'm in good health and physical condition minus my shoulder.   

**History:** No known trauma or event, but my right shoulder was hurting in 2008 when I was 29.  After an MRI my Ortho scheduled me for surgery to repair a labral tear. The day of surgery he found and repaired 3 tears (2 didn't show up on MRI) and 1 of the 3 was tied with a metal anchor. After PT and lifting weights I had full range of motion and strength back after 9 months. However, the aching was still present, especially when sleeping, and it never really went away. It got a little grouchier with age but never stopped me from being able to do anything.  Mostly it would just ache sometimes when sleeping.  Fast forward to last year.   I got in a bad car wreck that totaled my car and I thought I was ok other than some whiplash.  About 3 weeks later my shoulder started to hurt a lot and I couldn't lift my right arm over my head without a lot of pain. I got a steroid shot and then did 9 weeks of physical therapy. I had some increased range of motion and a little more strength but it still hurt a lot. I then got a Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) injection and was told to stop PT to let the injection work its magic. It was really sore afterwards and after another 3 weeks it just started hurting more.  I waited until about 7 weeks after the PRP injection and then got another steroid shot.  It helped a little bit, but nothing drastic. 

**Images:** Available at this link: [https://imgur.com/a/NVBQpHX](https://imgur.com/a/NVBQpHX)  There are 3 Xray images and 152 MRI images across 9 different MRI views. I left the image settings at the default in the medical image viewing programs, but if it would be helpful, I can export new versions of anything requested with the following options: Invert Contrast, Contrast Enhance, and Bone Enhance. The MRI results report is also included as an image.  No names or personal info is in any of the images.

**Xray findings:** Advanced glenohumeral joint space narrowing. Advanced acromial clavicular joint space narrowing with marginal osteophyte formation. No fracture or dislocation. No focal osseous lesions. Impression: Osteoarthritis.

**MRI findings:** It is one of the images in the photo album linked above.

**Orthopedic diagnosis:** My Ortho said the osteoarthritis is a 10 on scale where 10 is worst it can be. Here are a few quotes from him: "your shoulder is a train wreck", "your socket is just hanging open", "you have the shoulder of an 80-year-old". I mention that for context, not to discredit his bedside manner. I actually prefer things not be sugar coated and he is up front and realistic. Anyway, after all that, he said really my only options are a reverse total shoulder replacement or keep getting steroid shots every 6 weeks. I asked if more PT could help and he said it would just aggravate the osteoarthritis. With the shoulder replacement he said I would only get partial range of motion back and the procedure would have to likely be done again in 10-15 years as that is the shelf life for a shoulder replacement.

**My ask to this community:** Basically, my shoulder hurts all the time, makes grinding and popping noises, and I can't lift my right arm higher than the top of my rib cage without a lot of pain. On a scale of 10 the pain is 6 when I'm not doing anything and spikes to a 8 or 9 if I accidently raise my arm. I feel in a way I'm partially disabled/handicapped now as I can't do many things I could before all this started.  I really do not want to get replacement surgery since it won't give me the results I want, will cost a lot of money, and will only last 10-15 years.  I will go see another Dr. in person for a 2nd opinion but I also wanted to post here to see what others say to have more info to compare. My end goal is to have little to no pain, close to full ROM, and to be able to sleep at night without my shoulder waking me up all the time.

I was hoping someone could help me with the following questions:

1) Looking at the info and images, do you agree with the Ortho's prognosis that my socket really just "hanging open" and I have limited options? 

2) What would be your advice for a long-term solution to reach my goals listed above? Don't be shy to say replacement surgery if that seems like the best fit.

3) Any opinions on stem cell treatment? It sounded promising to me for re-growing cartilage and helping to heal wear and tear from what I've read, but I'd like to hear what the professionals here think about it.

title: Why don’t doctors try harder to diagnose chronically ill people?
selftext:
I (36F) have been on HMOs since I could finally afford insurance. So i need referrals to see specialists. Why have I spent 7 years begging doctors to take me seriously and begging to see specialists? Why is the only time I have gotten referrals if I, THE PATIENT, ask about random conditions that could be contributing. I have had 3 different PCPs and 5 different OBGYNs in the past 3 years because no one would listen to me. Why when I give my symptoms that are life-altering, do doctors run a basic blood chem and then when it’s mostly normals they just say, “bloodwork is good come back in 6 months if the symptoms that have been worsening for the past decade continue to worsen!”

I finally got a diagnosis of adenomyosis, possibly endometriosis after 4 ultrasounds, a CT, an MRI, drug trials, and an entire adult life of pain and suffering. 

I am still fighting to see an endocrinologist for: fatigue, temperature intolerance, migraines, joint pain, weight gain, hair loss, dry eyes, dry mouth, chronic yeast infections, intense anxiety, heart palpitations, dizziness, positional dizziness/heart palpitations, insomnia, acne, new heart murmur

I had to see gastro to have my gyno pain taken seriously. I have seen a cardiologist who basically did tests and I’m not dying I guess. I have been seeing a rheumatologist for 2 years who has been pushing me to see an endocrinologist. I have normal but steadily increasing inflammatory markers. Slightly high creatinine. Some mild elevation of APS markers on AVISE panel. 

My current primary agreed I should see an endocrinologist, but it has been a battle to get in anywhere due to office incompetence and reluctance of practitioners to take on new patients that don’t have a diagnosis of diabetes. 

I don’t use opioids nor have I ever asked for them despite my chronic pain especially related to my gyno issues. I do not want pain meds. I want to know what the hell is wrong with me. I am tired of every doctor just trying to treat individual symptoms rather than actually look at all my symptoms and figure out what is happening. I am so depressed from what I have been through. I am doing everything I can to feel better and am just getting worse. 

I go to pelvic floor PT, I go to therapy, I take my meds, I take my supplements, I try to sleep, I drink a gallon of water everyday, I have a healthy diet, I don’t eat out often, I don’t drink excessive caffeine, I don’t drink sugary drinks, I have minimal sugar intake. I try to go on walks everyday or a couple times a day since working out like I used to is physically impossible for me due to my abdominal pain, joint pain, and heart palpitations.

This process has been absolutely soul-crushing on top of being financially crippling. I live in a major metro area, I have decent insurance despite it being HMO. I dont understand why doctors never believe me or take me seriously. I am well spoken and educated. I was a vet tech for over a decade so I am not a laymen as far as medicine in general. I just want to understand why this is so hard.

title: MRI - History of Spina bifida and 10 years of chronic pain
selftext:
Age - 28

Sex - Female

Height - 5'4"

Weight- 7-8 stone

Race- Caucasian

Duration of complaint - 10 years

Location - neck, collar bone at the back, shoulder

Any existing relevant medical issues - IBS, chronic pain, depression, anxiety (my life is in pieces since, to be honest) cervical spina bifida at birth, surgery 2 weeks later and not seen anyone about it since. 

Current medications - buscopan, gabapentin

Include a photo if relevant - [Today's MRI](http://i.imgur.com/TrqJwdC.jpg)



November 2004 I fell at work and whacked my back, ever since I've had pain in the centre of my back (just where ribs end), burning pain between my shoulder and neck (which is eased sometimes by my partner pulling it back until it 'pops'), waves of intense pain in my neck which kinda crunches when i rotate it (mainly when i rotate my head left. I've finally got the strength to get this sorted and have some form of life again. 

So, top right image you can see that the spinal cord pokes out a bit, that is where I had surgery as a baby and also where a fair amount of the pain stems from.  I've got an appointment with the consultant next week but he's not very personable shall we say. 
Apologies for the potato quality, hopefully I'll be able to obtain copies next time.

title: OTC painkiller OD two weeks ago for extreme pain and needed to know gravity of the situation and if I should tell my PCP
selftext:
23yr afab 5'8 160ib
Hypermobile eds, raynauds, asthma, impacted teeth, food and general allergies, no known drug allergy
Rx: testosterone ethanate, zyrtec, vitamin D, adderall xr, cymbalta, albuterol, flonase

Severe tooth pain. Impacted wisdom tooth creating excessive pressure causing tooth beside it to pop slowly from pressue. All the while the other side towards the back of the mouth was growing into the bone of my mandible itself. Not a fun feeling. I have chronic pain and have been horribly fucked up many times in life. And only take meds if I have to. 

I hit a 9/10 on my pain scale. Even after excessive use of meds, oral lidocaine, ice, and antibiotic mouthwash. 

In the end I added up what I logged in my medication app to be:
-2,400mg of ibuprofen
-10,750mg of ibuprofen
-3 pepto chews
-20mg famotidine
-10mg zofran 

Mind u i didnt log one or two i think. So this may be a tad higher.

-stomach pain
-severe nausea
-vomiting
-excessive thirst
-shaking
-bruising
-headache
-abdominal pain
-acid reflux
-throat pain

Next day:
-nausea
-some stomach pain mildly 
-acid reflux
-aching and stabby pin in gut
-mild stomach pain
-dizziness

title: Something strange happened to me and my son that I still can’t figure out
selftext:
I am a 21 year old female and my son is nearly 2 years old. We are both healthy but maybe around 6 months ago we both went through something strange that a doctor was never really able to explain to me.

Me and my son had been at home all day while his father had been at work. Everything was normal, no signs of being sick, we hadn’t been around anyone sick, nothing that would make me think to watch out for any symptoms of illness in either one of us. I had ordered take out pizza in the middle of the day and both my son and I ate. An hour or so after I had eaten I noticed I was having cramps in my lower stomach. I thought they were normal menstrual cramps and waited for them to pass as usually the pain will come and then go away for me. I noticed though that it was lasting longer than usual, and the cramp kept getting higher in pain.

My son seemed fine and I had no other symptoms so I decided it was just a bad case of cramps and it would go away eventually. About an hour and a half later I realized something was off. The cramps had gotten so painful I had to go lay in my bed while my son watched cartoons in the living room not far away. His father was almost off and I called him to tell him that I was in pain and something wasn’t right and that I needed him to come home early to help me. That pain was horrible. I was nearly crying and I usually can take a lot of pain before it bothers me that much. 

As soon as I got off the phone with my partner my son walked into my room and I could see something just wasn’t right. He came up to the side of the bed and began vomiting. At that moment in my head I knew something must have been going on with both of us. I got up and comforted him and began trying to remove the sheets from my bed as I thought that was it and my son would be fine. But then I heard him walk out to the living room and start vomiting again. I ran out there to help him and as soon as I grabbed him I felt the strongest urge to vomit I have even felt in my life. I ran us to the bathroom and I emptied out my stomach and sat on the ground with my son laying in my arms. We were both exhausted and I knew something was horribly wrong. I waited on the ground for his father to get home and when he did I went to lay down with my son in my bed while his dad cleaned.

I waited for a few hours but the pain never went away and my son and I continued to occasionally vomit. I ended up deciding that we both neeeded to go to the hospital and as we were waiting there I could not stop puking. My son puked maybe two more times before passing out on his dad but I couldn’t stop being sick and when we were called into a room I needed a wheelchair to take me. I couldn’t stand up without doubling over and vomiting. The doctor ended up giving me an IV and some nausea medicine for my son. I was tested for covid and it came out negative and so did my son. The doctor could not give me a specific reason why we were sick, I suggested the pizza  gave us food poisoning and she told me that was too soon to make us that sick. She suggested something we had eaten earlier in the week had caused it, but she also mentioned something along the lines that my body may have just been reacting to my son becoming ill as sometimes a mother will develo the same symptoms of her sick child? Which didn’t make sense to me as I felt sick before even realizing something was wrong with him.

We both went home and my son did very well. He maybe had diarrhea for a few days but otherwise seemed normal. I did much worse. I continued to puke for a day or two and then for the rest of the week I continued having immense stomach pain and diarrhea. I got better obvioisly but I have never been that sick in my life. The pain was like nothing I had ever felt, maybe only almost comparable to cramps i had during my labor with my son.

To this day I have no idea what caused us to be sick. I thought food poisoning but then I noticed people I had been in contact with since like my partner and my mother  also came down with similar symptoms but to a much lesser extent. I also noticed that my grandmother who my son And I had had lunch with a week prior also became sick. If anyone has any ideas on what happened to us I would be interested to know! Thank you for your time!

title: 30f heart palpitations disabled me
selftext:
30f, 61-63kg, 174cm

No smoking, no drinking.

Have occasional migraines with auras (unmedicated)

For more than a year I’ve been having debilitating heart palpitation episodes that have disabled me — I had to quit my job, I cannot travel nor enjoy my life anymore and I’m even considering moving back to my parents. These palpitations are getting worse.

**the episodes look like this:**
The palpitations usually start at the evening. It starts with a few palpitations that are very strong, long and leave me breathless. 

After the initial palpitations, I start feeling a strong tension at the left side of my chest only. The ringing in my ears intensifies. I might also feel: dizzy, weak, difficulty to breathe. I get around 5-10 more strong palpitations during the episode. 

Usually it gets better in 1-3 hours, but sometimes the episodes are so bad and intense, I have to take a **propranolol** that my doctor prescribed me.

*I’ve been logging these episodes for half a year and I couldn’t find any significant similarities, just a few: 

they always happened 3-6 h after consuming caffeine (I don’t drink it anymore); 

More than a few times they happened 1-2 weeks before my period; 

More than a few times they occurred less than an hour after eating

Usually happened when I wasn’t being physically very active (eg when I was sitting, standing)*

——

**now, what the doctors have said:**

I had a cardiogram done and also wore a heart monitor. 

Cardiologist said it has recorded palpitations, but there’s nothing too unusual. The day I wore the monitor, I didn’t have the palpitation episode I described earlier. He told me to relax and prescribed propranolol.

My basic blood test was ok.

—-

My gp thinks this is just anxiety and I’m overreacting. However it’s just getting worse and ruining my life

title: Looking For Opinion: Massive Pain in Biceps & Inner Elbows, Progressively Getting Worse
selftext:
I am a 43 yo white male, approximately 6'2" and 230lbs. I am experiencing severe pain in both biceps, shoulders and inner elbows, similar to pain experienced after performing weight lifting curls (something I have not done in years). The pain is strong enough that lifting a cup of coffee is painful. There was no precipitating injury or activity. 

  The pain began in late October and was confined to my left shoulder and diagnosed as tendonapathy following a CT scan. I received cortisone shots to relieve the pain, which proved to be ineffective. The pain then spread to my right shoulder, in the same location, with the same level of pain.

The pain has gradually spread to my biceps and my inside elbows, the current terminus of the pain. I am treating the pain with a high dose of oxycodone, which is only mildly effective. I was also given an anti-inflammatory but it served to only make my fingers yellow from handling the pills.

As mentioned above, I have had a CT scan and have also been x-rayed. The x-rays were inconclusive. I am currently waiting on a pain management consult from the VA (unfortunately the rumors about long waiting lists are true and god knows when I will get into the clinic).

I am a Type II Diabetic and a Cancer Survivor (Non-Hodgkins Lymphoma) as of last November. I went through chemotherapy and radiation, with no known adverse reactions. I also have a surgically repaired disc, C6-7, which took 3 surgeries and 9 years to correct, the last being in 2009. I was also diagnosed with 2 additional discs in the process of rupturing (C5-6 and C7-T1), however MRIs performed at the VA failed to detect problems with those discs. Finally, in 2010 I had surgery to repair a torn rotator cuff and bicep in my right shoulder. I continue to have lingering pain from both surgically-corrected injuries. However, that pain is negligible compared to this latest pain.

I don't expect one of you to magically diagnose this issue and fix it. I would just like some opinions on the possible cause/s of this and courses of action. I have accepted the judgement of my local doctor and the VA for the past 4 or 5 months. But I can't do that anymore. What I'm experiencing is NOT normal and I'm afraid something is seriously wrong and want to take action now, rather than at their leisure.

Thank you for your time.

ian

P.S. I am retired from the U.S. Navy as of 2010. I am classified as 100% disabled and do not work.

title: Why do automated blood pressure cuffs measure my blood pressure so high? Can you refuse them?
selftext:
I am 30F female, 5”11 and 325lbs. Yes I know I’m plus size and I do have two chronic illnesses: Endometriosis and Vestibular Neuropathy (caused by a hemipelgic migraine when I was 21.) Both cause chronic pain and fatigue. I also have Covid induced POTS (I am vaccinated just unlucky with illnesses). For medications I take 50mg of Nortryptiline, 5mg of Aygestin, and Labetalol 10mg all before bed. I do have Indocin 75mg for Endo pain and migraine attacks. title: are taking NSAIDs every day ok for chronic pain?
selftext:
Hello,

I am 32F, I have an undiagnosed connective tissue disease, been experiencing symptoms since my teens, but been treated for 2 years and getting a 2nd opinion next week. I suffer from chronic pain and fatigue. I experience weakness and exhaustion after most exertion. I have a lot of lower back/hip pain and all over joint pain. I was improving and felt pretty good for a while. I am taking plaquenil and my blood results came back pretty normal recently.

Then after the holidays it took a down turn. I barely had the energy to do anything and still have to limit myself a lot or else my pain increases. My doctor recently suggested for me to take Ibprofen with Tylonel when my pain is at it's worst now. As it is, I take probably 6-10 ibprofen a day on top of plaquenil (2 times a day, 200mg each). Is this useage going to have a bad long term effect? I suppose it must be better than taking pain killers, but ?? I am just wondering if this is a long term solution or what anyone thinks on the matter. The ibprofen does work for me, but it does wear off. I got a bit nervous about introducing the tylonel. My blood results are pretty normal, which also makes it frustrating to identify what is going on, but if there was an issue with the NSAIDs would it appear in any blood results? I am just worried if 20-30+ more years of taking this volume is going to cause horrible effects.

Curious to hear what you think and also looking forward to the 2nd opinion of the new doctor. Thank you
